clue.text: When naked, I can be supreme creator

indicators.note: something naked has had its outer covering stripped off, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A boastful speaker claims that stripping off makes them feel like the creator of the universe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the chemical symbol for iodine; IODINE stripped of its outer letters leaves ODIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology Odin is the chief of the gods and helped shape the world, so he is a supreme creator.

clue.text: Chlorofluorocarbon said to protect small tree

indicators.note: the run of letters across the two words protects, or holds inside it, the word we want

parts.note: found inside, spanning the end of the long chemical name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A gas once used in aerosols is claimed, oddly, to shield a little tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it simply supplies the last three letters, joined to the final three of the chemical name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree grown in a pot and kept miniature by careful pruning, the Japanese art of dwarf trees.

clue.text: Single out car from 1989/90 that's blocking Seat Ateca, essentially

indicators.note: something blocking a road sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Spanish car maker, taken as written
a UK car registered from August 1989 to July 1990 had a G prefix, so it was a G reg

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very heart, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter model name

explanation.surface: Someone picks out an old motor that is parked in the way of a modern Seat Ateca SUV.
explanation.walkthrough: British number plates once began with a year letter; G covered 1989 to 1990. G REG sits inside SEAT, followed by the middle of ATECA.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart or isolate from the rest, which is what singling out does.

clue.text: Careless husband down with friends from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and going up

explanation.surface: A husband feeling low gets a bit sloppy when his mates from down south visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string husband-down-friends is read upwards, so the friends end up first.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and without care, so it is a synonym of careless.

clue.text: Cockney's announced right good look at biased information

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, and a Cockney Londoner drops final R sounds, so the words are judged by ear in that accent

parts.note: proper means thoroughly or right good in British slang, said by a Cockney without the R
a gander is a look, and the Cockney drops the final R

explanation.surface: An East Ender announces that it is time to have a really good look at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper gander' is British slang for a really good look; in a Cockney mouth it comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often misleading, spread to promote a political cause or point of view.

clue.text: Sleep with love god, taken from behind, leading to ulcer

parts.note: to bed someone is to sleep with them

indicators.note: taking something from behind means starting at its back end, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A risqué tale of a night with Cupid that ends unpleasantly with a sore.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as saucy, but 'taken from behind' is only an instruction to read the god's name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsore is an ulcer of the skin caused by lying in one position for too long.

clue.text: Everyone in fancy dance

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a fancy is a horse you back, and to fancy a result is to bet on it

explanation.surface: The whole cast is in an elaborate dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the dance but is a noun for a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a classical theatrical form of dance performed to music.

clue.text: Edge around gloomy devoted worshipper

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the lip of a cup is its edge

explanation.surface: A sombre, devout believer is walking round the edge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim travels to a holy place out of religious devotion, a committed worshipper.

clue.text: Treaty stored on phone

indicators.note: words heard over a phone line are only heard, never seen, so spelling does not matter

explanation.surface: A copy of an international agreement is kept on someone's mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties, the same thing as a treaty.

clue.text: Tempting Muslim missing first love

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word loses a letter

parts.note: the Moors were Muslims of North Africa and Spain
love is zero, written as O; the first of the two Os goes

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted by a Muslim who has lost their first sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means O in tennis scores, and 'first' picks which O leaves. The answer is a variant spelling of moreish.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreish, British informal, describes food so tasty that you want more of it: tempting.

clue.text: Golf course in German port?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a seaside golf course
second meaning: the German word for left, and port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is a golf course in some harbour town in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German port' suggests Kiel or Hamburg; it means the German word for port, the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are coastal golf courses, and in German links means left, the side a sailor calls port.

clue.text: Prepare to turn around one hundred baking sheets

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the rearranged letters surround the others
turning the letters over changes their order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cook gets ready to flip about a hundred sheets for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PREPARE wraps round I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is an edible thin sheet laid under macaroons and similar bakes to stop them sticking.

clue.text: Trying to get flat just before bedtime?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: smoothing something out or making it level
second meaning: the latter part of the day

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to find an apartment at the last minute before they go to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests a home; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a surface is evening it, and evening is the end of the day before people go to bed.

clue.text: Stock additional tonic supply

indicators.note: read as supple, adverb of supple, the letters are bent into new shapes

explanation.surface: An order for more tonic water to restock the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is read as 'supplely', in a pliable way, so the letters bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock and extraction both mean ancestry or descent, as in a person of Irish stock or extraction.

clue.text: Groups crossing English river

indicators.note: one thing crossing another is held across its middle, so one piece sits inside

explanation.surface: Bands of people are fording an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India, flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Tear up about row with a Parisian making escape

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so other letters are placed inside
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to row is to oar a boat

explanation.surface: A furious argument in which a Frenchman rips something up before fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed tear splits to hold the other pieces. To do a runner is British slang for leaving without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a runner is slang for bolting, typically from a restaurant without paying, so it means making an escape.

clue.text: Instructions for Countdown: Make sure you win!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a countdown runs to zero and halts

explanation.surface: Advice to a contestant on the TV quiz Countdown on how to come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV words-and-numbers quiz, but here a countdown is simply counting to zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop at nothing is to be ready to do anything at all to succeed; a countdown also halts at zero.

clue.text: Physical appearance of Sham 69's leader knocking out tenor

indicators.note: knocking someone out of a contest means taking their place, so one letter replaces another
the leader of something is at its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: sixty-nine, spelt out, starts with S

explanation.surface: A music writer on the look of the frontman of punk band Sham 69 shoving out a tenor singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sham 69 is a British punk band, but the clue splits them: S replaces T in PRETENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence can mean a person's bearing or impressive physical appearance, as in a commanding stage presence.

clue.text: Spoil home with a basin that's enclosed

parts.note: being in is being at home
taken as written; with joins it

explanation.surface: Someone ruins the house by fitting a sink that is boxed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basin' looks like a bathroom fitting, but here it is a dock for boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a sheltered harbour basin with moorings for yachts and small boats.

clue.text: Snobbish hostess not typically welcoming

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: found inside, spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A stuck-up hostess who is unusually unfriendly to guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Snotty is informal for superior or arrogant, the attitude of someone who looks down on others.

clue.text: Gave in when producing Mexican plants

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered when they finally grew some cacti-like plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave in' looks like the phrase for surrendering; the two words must be split, with 'in' as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaves are spiky succulents native to Mexico, the source of tequila and sisal.

clue.text: Chorus of "Desist!"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a repeated part of a song
second meaning: hold back, as a command

explanation.surface: A crowd shouting 'Stop!' together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chorus of' suggests many voices; it is a song's repeated section.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the recurring lines of a song, and to refrain is to abstain from doing something.

clue.text: Wonderful times eating bit of lamb fat

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: as in three by four, three times four

explanation.surface: Great fun eating fatty lamb chops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' is the multiplication word, as in a room twelve by ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means soft, loose and fleshy, so as an adjective it describes someone fat.

clue.text: Pub on island in Italian city

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island; on means placed after

explanation.surface: A drinking spot on an island off a southern Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a port city on the Adriatic coast of southern Italy, capital of Apulia.

clue.text: Mostly at sea?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: generally, for the most part
second meaning: out on the ocean, the main being an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' suggests confused; the main is a poetic word for the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main is an idiom meaning on the whole, and the main is an old literary term for the sea.

clue.text: Slightly over medium range

indicators.note: the phrase is spread over the other letter, covering it on both sides

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A cooking or clothing note: a range just a touch above medium.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIT is split to take the M between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or extent, the range within which something operates.

clue.text: Tied up detective

definitions.meaning: second meaning: old British slang for a police detective

explanation.surface: A detective has been bound with rope.
explanation.walkthrough: A busy, or busie, is dated British underworld slang for a plain-clothes detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy means occupied, as tied up does, and in British slang a busy is a police detective.

clue.text: American Express can get one a South American rodent

parts.note: to couch is to express in words, as in couched in polite terms

explanation.surface: Someone with an American Express card can buy themselves an exotic pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Express' looks like the credit card; split, Express means to word something.
explanation.definitionFit: The acouchi is a small agouti-like rodent from the forests of tropical South America.

clue.text: Important mission regenerating assembly line abandoned

indicators.note: regenerating means forming anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order
something abandoned is left behind, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A factory production line is scrapped in a vital rebuilding project.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission headed by an ambassador, an important one in a foreign capital.
